recentItems.title: Why being bisexual made me feel invisible | Iris Muche | TEDxDonauinsel Salon
recentItems.description:
What if the confusion isn't the problem, but the expectation that you must choose? In this deeply personal TEDx talk, Iris Muche explores bisexual invisibility, belonging, and why embracing life's spectrum is more powerful than fitting into a binary. 

https://www.irismuche.com  

Iris Muche is a psychosocial counsellor, trainer, and author. In 2021, she launched the blog "Die Max Mustermann" to inspire people to stop living their lives as placeholders waiting for something to happen, but rather to live self-determined lives guided by their own values. True to the motto: because your normal matters too! 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: You Might Be A Racist | Karla West | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description: Racism isn't always depicted by blatant beliefs, thoughts, and actions. It is often found in subtle mannerisms and deeds that may be considered commonplace. However, blatant or subtle, racism is wrong and must be first confronted within oneself in judgement. All people are to be celebrated and diversity makes the world beautiful. Karla F. West has always been a staunch supporter and advocate of peace and respect for all people by actively increasing awareness and celebration of all people as a Minister, Mediator and conflict resolution specialist, a Life Coach and Divorce Coach. She holds a BS in Human Services Management and a MA in Christian Ministry and is a TEDx ThirdWard speaker. She also serves as a Women’s Pastor and is a member of several organizations promoting peace and civil rights. She is the proud mother of three adult children and a doting grandmother. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How to live a good life in media | Mark Deuze | TEDxAU College
recentItems.description:
In mapping and analyzing issues at work that impact media workers' mental health and well-being, a paradoxical conclusion emerges: what makes media work special is also what can make its people sick. Drawing on his research Mark Deuze explores the challenges of living a good life in media. 
 Mark Deuze is Professor of Media Studies at the University of Amsterdam, author of 14 books (including "Life in Media" with The MIT Press), and bass player of the band Skinflower. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Who gets to define you? Identity in a world that classifies | Byron Adams | TEDxAU College
recentItems.description: Byron Adams examines how people understand and negotiate who they are across cultures, particularly in contexts of inclusion and marginalization, with the aim of translating research into more inclusive organizations and societies. Byron G. Adams is an Assistant Professor in Psychology at the University of Amsterdam, the Netherlands, and a Senior Research Associate in the Department of Industrial Psychology and People Management at the University of Johannesburg, South Africa. He is an identity psychologist whose work examines how people understand and negotiate who they are across cultures, particularly in contexts of inclusion and marginalization, with the aim of translating research into more inclusive organizations and societies. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: It’s time for a global constitution | Joyeeta Gupta | TEDxAU College
recentItems.description: Drawing on her award winning research, Joyeeta Gupta proposes the development of a global constitution. Through her talk she outlines her vision for a novel multilateral agreement that seeks to address the pressing challenges of today. Joyeeta Gupta is Professor of Environment and Development in the Global South at the University of Amsterdam and Professor at IHE-Delft Institute for Water Education. She received much of prestigious academic recognition, such as the Spinoza prize in 2023 (the highest academic recognition in the Netherlans), the Amsterdam Impact Prize in 2025 and the 2022 Piers Sellers Prize for climate research. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why we should stop optimizing ourselves | Franka Baum | TEDxAU College
recentItems.description: Taking from her experience as a young person surrounded by social media, Franka challenges the notion of self-optimization. She argues for a new paradigm in which we stop treating our lives as projects needing to be improved. Franka Baum from Germany is a first-year social sciences student focusing on international relations and political science. She is particularly interested in politics and in understanding human agency and behavior.
